newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean non-life insurers' profits plunge.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean non-life insurers' profits plunge.

text.p: After-tax net profits of South Korea's non-life insurers plunged in the year to March due to increased underwriting losses and operating expenses, the Korea Non-life Insurance Association said on Thursday.
Net profits of the 17 non-life insurers operating in South Korea amounted to 56.16 billion won in the year, down from a 132.74 billion won profit a year earlier, the association said.
Their premium income during the year rose 21.3 percent to 14.40 trillion won from the previous year's 11.87 trillion, data released by the association showed.
But their underwriting losses widened by 46.4 percent to 1.01 trillion won from 690.11 billion won in the year ending in March 1996, the data showed.
Their net operating expenses rose by a sharp 44.9 percent to 3.39 trillion won from 2.34 trillion a year earlier.
Samsung Fire and Marine Insurance Co, the largest in terms of premium income, posted a net profit of 12.36 billion won in the year versus a 12.13 billion won profit a year before.

Hyundai Marine and Fire Insurance Co saw its net profit fall to 6.02 billion won from 7.02 billion and LG Insurance Co's net profit fell to 3.05 billion won from 3.72 billion, the association's data showed.
Oriental Fire Marine Insurance Co posted a net profit of 13.95 billion won in the year, up sharply from a 5.71 billion won profit a year earlier.
